6 itineraries

SlovakiaOne day on foot

Bratislava

Urban House brunch, Old Town wandering, castle views and dinner to suit the mood.

Open the itinerary ↗

Bratislava · at a glance

Highlights

  • Bratislava Castle and its views over the Danube
  • The pastel-blue Blue Church
  • Old Town lanes, St Martin’s Cathedral and Čumil
  • Coffee, cake and a riverside stroll
Best months
May–June and September (December for the Christmas markets)
Getting around
Compact and walkable: about 25 minutes on foot from the main station.
Good to know
Paid in euros. An easy day trip from Vienna, about an hour by train.
Open the itinerary ↗
Austria3-week stay

Vienna

Three weeks of exploring, arranged into four suggested days plus extra museum stops.

Open the itinerary ↗

Vienna · at a glance

Highlights

  • Schönbrunn Palace and the Gloriette
  • Klimt at the Upper Belvedere
  • St Stephen’s Cathedral and the Hofburg
  • Coffee houses, Naschmarkt and a Heuriger evening
Best months
May–June and September (December for the Christmas markets)
Getting around
U-Bahn and trams go everywhere; a weekly pass covers most stays.
Good to know
Book timed tickets for Schönbrunn and the Belvedere ahead. Paid in euros.
Open the itinerary ↗
Mexico2 weeks · flexible

Mexico City

Slow afternoons, neighbourhood wandering, good food and two Saturday adventures.

Open the itinerary ↗

Mexico City · at a glance

Highlights

  • Centro Histórico, Templo Mayor and the murals
  • Chapultepec Castle and the big museums
  • Frida’s Coyoacán
  • A day at the Teotihuacán pyramids
Best months
February–March and November
Getting around
Walk the neighbourhoods; Metro or a rideshare for longer hops.
Good to know
The city sits at 2,240 m: go easy on day one and bring a layer for cool evenings.
Open the itinerary ↗
Mexico2 weeks · planned

San Miguel de Allende

Rooftop coffees, cobbled wandering, a cooking class and two Saturdays out: Guanajuato, then horses and hot springs.

Open the itinerary ↗

San Miguel de Allende · at a glance

Highlights

  • The Parroquia and Jardín Allende
  • El Charco del Ingenio and Fábrica La Aurora
  • A pyramid and a vineyard lunch
  • Guanajuato, horses and hot springs
Best months
November and February–March
Getting around
Steep cobbles on foot (comfy shoes!), taxis for the day trips.
Good to know
Check opening days: several favourites close early in the week. Winter nights get chilly.
Open the itinerary ↗
VietnamAbout a month

Vietnam

Phu Quoc, Hanoi, Ninh Binh, Ha Long Bay, the Ha Giang Loop and Hoi An.

Open the itinerary ↗

Vietnam · at a glance

Highlights

  • Hanoi’s Old Quarter and street food
  • Ninh Binh by boat and the Hang Mua viewpoint
  • A Ha Long Bay cruise and the Ha Giang Loop
  • Lantern nights in Hoi An
Best months
March–April (September–October is the trickiest time for this route)
Getting around
Domestic flights for long hops; limousine vans, sleeper buses and Grab locally.
Good to know
Check visa rules before you book. Carry some cash (đồng) for markets and street food.
Open the itinerary ↗
JapanAbout a month

Japan for first-timers

Tokyo, Kyoto, Osaka and a weekend in Takayama, with room to take it slowly.

Open the itinerary ↗

Japan for first-timers · at a glance

Highlights

  • Tokyo: Senso-ji, Shibuya and Meiji Shrine
  • Kyoto: Fushimi Inari, Kiyomizu-dera and Arashiyama
  • Osaka Castle, Dotonbori and Nara’s deer
  • Mount Fuji and a Takayama weekend
Best months
Cherry blossom season (late March–April), May and October–November
Getting around
Trains everywhere: an IC card for city transit and the Shinkansen between cities.
Good to know
Book cherry-blossom stays and popular experiences early. Cash is still handy.

Support local women

If you can afford to and would like to, consider supporting a women’s shelter in one of these destinations.

I don’t receive any money or commission from these donations. Supporting local women matters to me, and this is one small way to give back to the places I visit. It takes all of us to stand against gender-based and domestic violence.

  • Vienna, Austria — Donate to Wiener Frauenhäuser ↗
  • Mexico City, Mexico — Donate to Red Nacional de Refugios ↗
  • Vietnam — Donate to Peace House Shelters ↗
  • Japan — Donate to All Japan Women’s Shelter Network ↗
  • Bratislava, Slovakia — Donate to Brána do života ↗
